extracted.intended_audience: writers entering the NYC Midnight Flash Fiction Challenge (flash fiction contest participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing an original flash fiction (short story) to submit to the NYC Midnight Flash Fiction Challenge under time-limited, prompt-driven rules (genre, location, object) with rounds of judging and advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limit (no longer than 1,000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have 48 hours to craft an original short story no longer than 1,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly states stories must be "no longer than 1,000 words." Entrants should ensure their submission does not exceed this limit; entries are judged within this constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit (48 hours per round)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have 48 hours to craft an original short story for each round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each round (1st, 2nd, Final) gives writers 48 hours from assignment to submit. Plan time-management accordingly; submissions created outside the 48-hour window would violate the contest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned genre requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be written in the assigned genre provided with the prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the 1st Round, writers are assigned a genre (along with location and object) and must write within that genre. Judges will evaluate against peers who received the same prompt/genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned location must be a predominant location
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must use the assigned location as a predominant location in their story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The location assignment must be a prominent setting element — not merely a passing mention. The page phrase: "using the assigned location as a predominant location in their story."

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned object must physically appear
rubrics_metrics.description: The assigned object must physically appear at some point in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The object must be present within the narrative ("having their object physically appear at some point"). It should be integrated clearly enough that judges can confirm the requirement is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (story must be original)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be original short stories created by the entrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes "original short story" for each round; reuse, plagiarism, or submitting previously published work would conflict with this requirement (see Official Rules for full details).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI prohibition for writers (no AI in creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are explicitly prohibited from using AI in the creation of their story, in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: "We have specific rules against writers using AI in the creation of their story (see Official Rules paragraph 20. D) in whole or in part." Entrants should consult the Official Rules for the exact language and enforcement details. Noncompliance may lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI prohibition for judges (judges must not use AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges are not allowed to use AI when reviewing submissions or providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page says: "No. We have a strict policy against judges using AI in the review of the stories. We check every judge, every round, to determine the likelihood of AI use. If we ever found a judge using AI ... we would never use that judge again." This is an enforcement and integrity standard for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and comparative judging (same-prompt groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are placed randomly into groups that receive the same exact prompt; judges score stories only against others within the same group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A group consists of writers who received the same exact prompt assignment. "Judges will only score the stories against others within the same group to determine which stories advance to the next round." This means evaluation is comparative among same-prompt peers rather than absolute across the whole field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement criteria by round (top selections advance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancement is determined by judges selecting a set number of top stories per group each round: top seven advance from 1st to 2nd Round; top three advance from 2nd Round to Final Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: "The judges choose a top seven from each group to advance to the 2nd Round... Judges select the top three writers in each group from the 2nd Round to advance to the Final Round." Entrants should be aware that only a small subset advances each round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback provided for every submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges provide feedback for every submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page promises feedback for every submission and additional peer-review opportunities in a special review forum. Expect to receive judge comments even if you do not advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors retain rights to their stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers retain all rights to the stories they create during the competition; the organization will not share stories publicly without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site states: "Writers retain all the rights to the stories they create during the competition, which means that we could not and would not share the stories publicly without consent from the authors." This addresses copyright and distribution concerns (also tied to the AI-training statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Random assignment of prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers are placed randomly in groups and receive random assignments of genre, location, and object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes writers are "placed randomly in groups* and are assigned a genre, location, and object assignment." This is procedural but affects strategy — prompts are not chosen by entrants.
